title: CIDR
description: Classless addressing: any mask length you want
tagline: Classless addressing: any mask length you want

sections.title: What CIDR Means
sections.body: CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing) throws away fixed classes. Instead of "Class B" you write exactly how many bits are network: /22, /27 — anything. Format: IP/prefix, e.g. 10.1.1.0/22.

sections.title: Route Summarization Bonus
sections.body: CIDR also works upward: many small networks can be advertised as ONE bigger route — smaller routing tables, faster routers.

sections.title: Reading Any Prefix Fast
sections.body: For /X: host bits = 32 − X, usable hosts = 2^(32−X) − 2. Every CIDR question is just this one formula.
